dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An integral conservation-law predicate for a vector-valued field q and flux map f: on every real interval and at every time, q is interval integrable and the time derivative of its interval integral is f(q(a,t))−f(q(b,t)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the first hypothesis, asserting the global integral form of the conservation law for the embedded scalar field and constant-matrix flux.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constant 1×1 real matrix whose sole entry is speed.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the coefficient matrix used to define the linear flux.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Matrix-vector multiplication, mapping a coefficient matrix and state vector to coefficient.mulVec state.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the flux map in both the integral-law hypothesis and the first conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: An abbreviation for the pointwise scalar advection predicate LocalDef007 q speed x t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the second conjunct of the conclusion at every spatial point.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Embedding of a scalar field q(x,t) as a Fin 1 → Real vector whose unique component is q(x,t).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It lets the scalar field be supplied to the vector-valued integral conservation-law predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: A theorem furnishing continuous real scalar multiplication on real-valued function spaces.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the differentiability and continuity infrastructure used in the target.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: The pointwise advection equation predicate: there exist a time derivative q_t and spatial derivative q_x at (x,t) such that q_t + speed·q_x = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the exact scalar differential statement asserted at every x in the second conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: A theorem furnishing continuous real scalar multiplication on any real normed space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is analytic typeclass support for derivative statements used by LocalDef007.

binders: q : Real → Real → Real is a scalar field, with q(x,τ) interpreted as its value at spatial point x and time τ.
speed and t are real numbers.
qt, qx, and fluxx are functions from Real to one-component real vectors Fin 1 → Real, intended as chosen time derivatives, spatial derivatives, and spatial flux derivatives at the fixed time t.
hypotheses: The one-component embedding Q(x,τ)=(q(x,τ)) satisfies the integral conservation law with flux F(U)=A U, where A is the constant 1×1 matrix with entry speed: for every a,b,τ, Q(·,τ) is interval integrable and d/dτ ∫_a^b Q(x,τ) dx = F(Q(a,τ))−F(Q(b,τ)).
For every x, qt(x) is the derivative at time t of τ ↦ Q(x,τ).
For every x, qx(x) is the derivative at x of ξ ↦ Q(ξ,t).
For every x, fluxx(x) is the derivative at x of ξ ↦ F(Q(ξ,t)).
qt is interval integrable on every real interval.
fluxx is interval integrable on every real interval.
For every a and b, at time t the derivative of τ ↦ ∫_a^b Q(x,τ) dx is ∫_a^b qt(x) dx.
The one-component-vector-valued residual x ↦ qt(x)+fluxx(x) is continuous.
conclusions: For every state U : Fin 1 → Real, the constant-matrix flux satisfies F(U)(j)=speed·U(0) for the unique component j.
For every real x, q satisfies the scalar advection equation at (x,t): there exist real values q_t and q_x that are respectively the time and space derivatives of q there and obey q_t + speed·q_x = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Q(x,τ) is the one-component vector with Q(x,τ)(0)=q(x,τ).
A is the 1×1 matrix A(i,j)=speed, and F(U)=A.mulVec U.
The integral conservation law uses the oriented interval integral and the endpoint flux difference F(Q(a,τ))−F(Q(b,τ)).
The pointwise advection predicate at (x,t) is ∃ q_t q_x, HasDerivAt (τ ↦ q(x,τ)) q_t t ∧ HasDerivAt (ξ ↦ q(ξ,t)) q_x x ∧ q_t+speed·q_x=0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Assume a scalar field, embedded as a one-component system with constant linear flux of speed times state, satisfies the integral conservation law and enough differentiability, interval-integrability, differentiation-under-the-integral, and continuity hypotheses at a fixed time. Then the matrix flux is explicitly speed times the unique state component, and the field satisfies q_t + speed q_x = 0 at every spatial point at that time.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion is conditional on strong analytic hypotheses, including a global-in-time integral conservation law and a separately assumed differentiation-under-the-integral identity.
The pointwise PDE conclusion is only at the single bound time t, although the integral conservation-law hypothesis quantifies over all times.
No initial condition, boundary condition, uniqueness, existence interval, or propagation formula is asserted.
No restriction on the sign or magnitude of speed is imposed.
The result is fixed to a one-component state space Fin 1 → Real.

The derivative fields qt, qx, and fluxx are assumed to exist everywhere at the fixed time; their relationships follow through derivative uniqueness and the integral argument rather than being primitive data equations.
No numerical discretization, approximation error, stability, or convergence property is involved.
ambiguities: The variable names suggest time and space roles, but those roles are determined only by the argument positions and derivative hypotheses.
The proposition uses the library's oriented interval integral conventions; no separate convention is specified in the dossier.
